brief: WSJ and NYT reports say NVIDIA's board is preparing to part ways with founding CEO Jensen Huang after a previously reported relationship with an alleged Chinese spy, compounded by new allegations of a relationship with an NVDA executive; Oppenheimer calls this a "one-two punch" that forced the board's hand. Citing no obvious successor and risk of a "brain drain" that threatens NVDA's pace of innovation, Oppenheimer downgrades NVDA to Perform and removes its $315 price target. It still sees upside to the F3Q (Oct.) print and F4Q outlook when NVDA reports Tuesday 11/17, but expects fundamentals to take a backseat near term because the departure could create a lingering share overhang; it maintains CY26/27/28E EPS at $9.40/$16.84/$23.27 pending clarity. Perceived beneficiaries of any NVDA dislocation: AMD, MRVL, AVGO. Supporting detail: datacenter (93% of sales) seen up 14% Q/Q (+99% Y/Y) on ramping VR200 shipments; gross margin modeled to bottom at 71.7% in F4Q before expanding into CY28; buybacks have returned ~60% of FCF to shareholders YTD versus a 50% target. NVDA is down 7% YTD versus the SOX's +49%, trading at 7x CY28E EPS versus its 3-/5-year average of 21x/25x.
